To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nicotine patch can reduce smoking and alcohol consumption in alcoholics.
the nicotine patch was not effective in reducing the number of cigarettes smoked per day, and the number of cigarettes per day did not change over the 6 weeks of treatment.
the efficacy of the nicotine patch is similar in smokers with a past history of alcoholism and smokers without such a history.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and evaluation of an integrated approach for the analysis of the efficacy of the nicotine patch in smoking cessation, which takes account of the fact that smoking and drinking are inter-related.
the efficacy of nicotine patch therapy for smokers with a history alcoholism.
the development of a nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) for the treatment of tobacco addiction, which is based on a novel nicotine patch.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for the efficacy of nicotine replacement therapy in the treatment of alcoholism is not conclusive and the evidence for its use is not strong.

the use of the nicotine patch in smokers who have a history of alcohol abuse is not associated with an increased risk for relapse to alcohol use and is not associated with increased alcohol consumption in those smokers who relapse.
nicotine patch treatment of smoking cessation is effective and safe for smokers with a history or current alcohol abuse or dependence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nicotine patch is an effective and safe aid to smoking cessation in smokers with and without a history of alcohol abuse or dependence.
nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) is effective in promoting abstinence from smoking, and the effect is independent of the presence of a history of alcohol abuse.
nicotine patch is effective in helping smokers with a history alcoholism to abstain from smoking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of nicotine replacement and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a promising treatment for smokers with a history alcoholism.
the nicotine patch is effective in helping people quit smoking, even those who have a history of alcohol dependence.
the nicotine patch may not be the best treatment for smokers who also have a history of alcohol use.
